title: Every system call on six hardware designs
summary: Eleven logical programs (memories, Deutsch–Jozsa, Bell pairs, a Z⊗Z merge, GHZ, a checked measurement, T injection, a loop of merges, at distances 3 and 5) on two designs of each platform. For every system call, the time each operation actually needed on the cycle-exact model, against the one number the machine declares.
method: For each program and design, the compiler lowers the program against a machine specification, its resource VM admits the listing, and the listing runs time-triggered on the design. Every duration the hardware exceeded is raised and the loop repeats until the run conforms. The final run's operations are the samples.
65 runs conform. measurement-d3 on ions-qccd: listing line 143: zone of the route's hub is full (12 ions, capacity 12; the route gathers 13; others there: ).
findings: Routes on atoms need 73 to 183 µs and on ions 0.87 to 1.25 ms; the declared route latency must be the longest, so the median route carries 90 µs (atoms) and 0.2 ms (ions) the hardware does not use.
Readout lengths differ per transmon (1.0 to 1.4 µs on the generated chip's calibration): the declared measurement is the longest.
The decoder's median decode is a fifth of its worst; the worst is what a single latency must say.
